h1: The 6 Best Mount-It! Standing Desk Converters for Every Screen Setup, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 Mount-It! desk converters, from compact gas-spring risers to dual and triple monitor models, compared on size and lift.
summary: The Mount-It! 32 x 22 inch gas-spring converter is the best all-round pick, with a standard-sized platform and the brand's simple lift. The dual-monitor model suits two-screen desks, the 30 inch compact is the budget entry, and the triple-monitor electric unit is the heavy-duty option for three displays.
intro: Mount-It! started in monitor arms and wall mounts, and that heritage shows in how its converters are built. Where many rivals sell a plain platform, this brand tends to attach the monitor mounts directly to the unit, which solves a problem most buyers do not see until later: where do the screens go when the platform rises?

We ranked six Mount-It! converters, from compact risers to a triple-monitor electric model. They split into three groups: standard and compact gas-spring platforms, models with integrated monitor mounts, and one motorized unit. We checked platform size, lift type, mount design and price tier, and we are open about the many details Mount-It! leaves off these listings, such as weight capacity and height range.

products.name: Mount-It! Standing Desk Converter 32 x 22, Sit Stand Desk Riser with Gas Spring Lift
products.verdict: A 32 by 22 inch gas-spring platform, the standard-sized Mount-It! converter.
products.description:
This Mount-It! converter has a 32 by 22 inch platform and a gas-spring lift, in the $100 to $200 range. A 22 inch depth is the number that matters: it is deep enough for a monitor and a keyboard to share the surface without crowding.

It is the top pick here because it makes the fewest compromises. The platform is large enough for a laptop and a monitor, or a monitor and keyboard, and the gas spring lets one hand raise and lower it. It costs less than the monitor-mount models and works on most desks. It lacks integrated mounts, so monitors sit directly on the platform.

Buy it for a standard one-monitor desk. If you run multiple screens, the integrated mount models are better.
products.idealFor: One-monitor desks needing a standard, reliable converter.
products.skipIf: You run two or three monitors.

products.name: Mount-It! Standing Desk Converter Dual Monitor, 2 Screen Mounts Included
products.verdict: Integrated dual-monitor mounts keep both screens off the work surface.
products.description:
This Mount-It! converter includes integrated mounts for two monitors, and costs $200 to $500. The mounts attach to the converter itself, so your displays rise and fall together with the keyboard platform.

It ranks second because mounting screens on arms frees the work surface and keeps the screens at a consistent distance from your eyes. For a two-screen desk, this is a cleaner setup than a flat platform with monitors on stands. The extra cost is meaningful, and the listing gives no platform size or load limit, so check the dimensions against your displays.

Buy it if you use two monitors daily. Take the 32 by 22 model if you have one screen.
products.idealFor: Two-monitor desks that need tidy, adjustable screens.
products.skipIf: You only use a single monitor.

products.name: Mount-It! Height Adjustable Standing Desk Converter, Compact 30 Inch Wide Tabletop
products.verdict: A 30 inch wide gas-spring tabletop, the cheapest way into the brand.
products.description:
This model has a 30 inch wide tabletop with a gas-spring lift, priced between $100 and $200. It is the narrowest of the standard-sized models here.

Third place reflects a balance. It costs about the same as the 32 by 22 and has two inches less width, and the listing gives no depth, which keeps it behind. Its strength is that it fits smaller desks and stays in the Mount-It! family for parts and support.

Buy it for a small desk with one monitor. If you can spare the room, the 32 by 22 is a better surface.
products.idealFor: Small desks with a single monitor or a laptop.
products.skipIf: You want a deep working surface.

products.name: Mount-It! Triple Monitor Electric Standing Desk Converter, 3 Screens
products.verdict: Triple monitor mounts and an electric lift for large multi-screen desks.
products.description:
The triple monitor model combines mounts for three screens with an electric lift, priced from $200 to $500. A motor does the lifting, which matters when three monitors and a keyboard add up to a heavy load.

It sits fourth because it is the most specialized unit and the listing says nothing about platform size or capacity. A motor suits a heavy multi-screen load much better than a gas spring, and the mounts keep the screens organized. The catch is that the listing carries the weakest feedback of the group, which makes reliability a question.

Buy it if you truly use three monitors and want a motor. Check the warranty and the weight limit first.
pros: Keeps screens at a steady height
products.idealFor: Triple-monitor setups that need a motor.
products.skipIf: You want proven reliability or fewer screens.

products.name: Mount-It! Standing Desk Converter, Compact Design
products.verdict: A compact gas-spring converter with almost no printed detail.
products.description:
Mount-It! sells this as a compact converter lifted by a gas spring. Neither the width nor the price tier appears in the data we reviewed, which leaves the retailer page as your only source for dimensions.

Fifth place is about information. The gas-spring mechanism is a good fit for a small platform, and the brand is dependable, but a buyer should be able to compare width and depth. A missing price tier also prevents us from judging value.

Buy it if you want a small Mount-It! converter and verify the measurements. The 30 inch tabletop is clearer and costs about the same.
cons: No width or price tier listed
products.idealFor: Small desks where the buyer will check dimensions.
products.skipIf: You want clear specs up front.

products.name: Mount-It! Compact Standing Desk Riser, Height Adjustable Desktop Sit Stand Workstation
products.verdict: A compact gas-spring workstation riser at a higher price than the 30 inch model.
products.description:
The compact riser is a height adjustable desktop sit-stand workstation with a gas-spring lift, priced between $200 and $500. It is aimed at smaller desks.

Sixth place comes from value. It costs well above the 30 inch tabletop and the 32 by 22, and the listing offers no size or capacity numbers to justify that. The ergonomic design and brand are positives, but a buyer pays more for the same lift type.

Buy it only if you have confirmed a feature on the retailer page that you need. Otherwise choose the cheaper compact models.
products.idealFor: Buyers who confirm the specs justify the price.

methodology.title: Platform size
methodology.description: We compared stated platform dimensions, favouring depth as well as width, because depth sets how a monitor and keyboard share the surface.

methodology.title: Monitor mount integration
methodology.description: Converters with built-in dual or triple mounts scored for freeing the work surface and keeping screens at a steady distance.

methodology.title: Lift mechanism
methodology.description: Gas springs and electric motors were compared for effort, load handling and the added failure risk of a motor.

methodology.title: Listing completeness
methodology.description: Models that state a size, lift type and price tier ranked above those where basic specs are missing.

methodology.title: Price against features
methodology.description: Tiers of $100 to $200 and $200 to $500 were weighed against platform size and mounts to judge where the extra cost is justified.

whatMatters.detail: Depth is the front-to-back distance and decides how far your monitor sits from your eyes. A 22 inch depth gives you room for a keyboard in front of a monitor. Check the depth on the listing, since width alone does not tell you.

Built-in arms clamp your monitors to the converter, keeping them off the surface. This is cleaner and lets you adjust screen position. Confirm the mounts match your monitors' VESA hole pattern, usually 75 by 75 or 100 by 100 millimeters.

Gas springs lift by hand with a smooth pull but need effort with heavy loads. Electric lifts raise a heavy load at the push of a button and suit multi-screen setups. Electric units add a power cord and a motor that can fail.
The total weight of monitors, laptop and accessories must stay under the limit. Multi-monitor desks reach it quickly. Check the manufacturer page, since these listings often omit it.

The converter sits on your existing desk, so the desk has to support the extra weight and be wide enough for the base. A wobbly desk magnifies platform shake. Measure the desk surface before choosing.

howToChoose.intro: The number of screens you run decides which Mount-It! converter makes sense, so begin there.

cards.label: Gas spring
cards.text: Springs counterbalance the load so you can raise the platform with one hand. Most Mount-It! converters here use this, including the 32 x 22 and the 30 inch tabletop.

cards.label: Electric
cards.text: A motor lifts the platform at the push of a button. The Triple Monitor Electric model is the one motorized option, built for heavy multi-screen loads.

howToChoose.note: Choose gas spring for one or two light monitors, and electric only for three screens or very heavy gear.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Built-in mounts that match your screens, a stated weight limit and a lift that holds heavy loads. Cable management stops wires from snagging when the platform moves.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Dual Monitor model suits two displays, and the Triple Monitor Electric handles three. Both attach the screens to the converter.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You use several monitors daily and want them to rise with the keyboard. The $200 to $500 Dual and Triple models are built for it.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have one monitor or a laptop. The 32 x 22 and 30 inch models cost $100 to $200 and do the job.

faq.q: Will the monitor mounts fit my screens?
faq.a: They fit monitors with a standard VESA pattern, usually 75 by 75 or 100 by 100 millimeters. Check the back of your monitor. Very large or curved screens may exceed the mount's limits.

faq.q: What is the common mistake with Mount-It! converters?
faq.a: Overlooking weight. Dual or triple monitors with arms add up fast, and a gas spring can struggle at the limit. Check the manufacturer's capacity before you load the platform.

faq.q: Is the electric model worth it over gas spring?
faq.a: For three monitors, yes. A motor handles heavy loads at the push of a button. For one or two light screens, a gas spring is simpler and cheaper.

faq.q: How do I set up a Mount-It! converter?
faq.a: Most arrive mostly assembled. Place the base on the desk, attach any monitor mounts, then load your screens last. Check the lift moves smoothly before adding the full weight.

faq.q: How do I care for a gas spring lift?
faq.a: Keep loads within the limit, avoid slamming the platform down and wipe the guides clean. Gas springs can weaken after years. Replacement parts are easier to find from an established brand.

faq.q: Can I use these on a glass desk?
faq.a: Use caution. Converters concentrate weight on small feet, which can scratch or stress glass. Put a protective pad under the base and check the desk's weight rating.

finalTake: The Mount-It! 32 x 22 gas-spring converter is the best all-round choice for most desks, and the 30 inch tabletop is the cheaper alternative for smaller spaces. If you run two monitors, the Dual Monitor model is the cleaner setup, while the Triple Monitor Electric handles three. The compact riser and Compact Design models need a spec check before you buy.
